body_facts.article_description: BBC Mundo reports Delcy Rodríguez as interim president, increasingly referred to in Venezuelan official communications as ‘president’, ‘national leader’ or ‘head of state’; article says only two communications called her ‘interim’ recently. It describes Maduro as captured in January and calls him former president/ex-president in narrative; attributes continuing ‘President Maduro’ language to Diosdado Cabello and some supporters.
body_facts.specific_reported_actions: Article reports Rodríguez did not mention Maduro in her UN General Assembly address, thanked President Trump for diplomatic relations/cooperation, changed cabinet figures, promoted hydrocarbons and amnesty laws, unlocked some digital media, and reached an oil agreement with the US. It reports replacement of Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino López and a complete change of the armed-forces leadership; these are journalistic assertions, not independently verified here against official instruments.
body_facts.attribution_and_limits: Article quotes/comments from journalists Valentina Gil (via TalCual), International Crisis Group analyst Phil Gunson, Cornell professor Irina Troconis, and Maynooth professor Maryhen Jiménez. Claims of deliberate erasure/rebranding, political consolidation, a ‘new coalition’, election avoidance, and its capacity to connect with society are attributed analysis, not formal acts or proof of legal succession. It says Rodríguez promised elections without a date or circumstances. This is a BBC publisher article, not government/UN primary evidence; it documents no appointment decree, term instrument, or current Maduro legal designation sourced to a primary record.
